questions.q: A gas balloon is going up with a constant velocity of $10$ m/s. When this balloon reached a height of $75$ m, a stone is dropped from it and balloon keeps moving up with the same velocity. The height of the balloon when the stone hits the ground is ________ m. (Take $g=10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.solution:
When the stone is dropped, it acquires the initial velocity of the balloon. Taking the upward direction as positive, the initial velocity of the stone is $u = 10$ m/s.

The displacement of the stone when it hits the ground is $S = -75$ m, and its acceleration is $a = -g = -10$ m/s$^2$.

Using the equation of motion $S = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^2$:

$-75 = 10t - \dfrac{1}{2}(10)t^2$

$-75 = 10t - 5t^2$

$5t^2 - 10t - 75 = 0$

$t^2 - 2t - 15 = 0$

$(t - 5)(t + 3) = 0$

Since time cannot be negative, $t = 5$ s.

During this time, the balloon continues to move upwards with a constant velocity of $10$ m/s. The distance travelled by the balloon in $5$ s is:

$d = v \times t = 10 \times 5 = 50$ m

The total height of the balloon when the stone hits the ground is:

$H = 75 + 50 = 125$ m

Answer: $125$

questions.q: Two masses of $3.4$ kg and $2.5$ kg are accelerated from an initial speed of $5$ m/s and $12$ m/s, respectively. The distances traversed by the masses in the $5^\text{th}$ second are $104$ m and $129$ m, respectively. The ratio of their momenta after $10$ s is $\dfrac{x}{8}$. The value of $x$ is ________.
questions.solution:
The distance traversed in the $n^{\text{th}}$ second is given by $S_n = u + \dfrac{a}{2}(2n - 1)$.

For the first mass ($m_1 = 3.4$ kg, $u_1 = 5$ m/s):
$104 = 5 + \dfrac{a_1}{2}(2 \times 5 - 1)$
$99 = \dfrac{9a_1}{2} \Rightarrow a_1 = 22$ m/s$^2$

For the second mass ($m_2 = 2.5$ kg, $u_2 = 12$ m/s):
$129 = 12 + \dfrac{a_2}{2}(2 \times 5 - 1)$
$117 = \dfrac{9a_2}{2} \Rightarrow a_2 = 26$ m/s$^2$

Velocities of the masses after $10$ s:
$v_1 = u_1 + a_1 t = 5 + 22 \times 10 = 225$ m/s
$v_2 = u_2 + a_2 t = 12 + 26 \times 10 = 272$ m/s

Momenta of the masses after $10$ s:
$p_1 = m_1 v_1 = 3.4 \times 225 = 765$ kg m/s
$p_2 = m_2 v_2 = 2.5 \times 272 = 680$ kg m/s

Ratio of their momenta:
$\dfrac{p_1}{p_2} = \dfrac{765}{680} = \dfrac{9}{8}$

Comparing with $\dfrac{x}{8}$, we get $x = 9$.

Answer: $9$

questions.q: The velocity ($v$) versus time ($t$) plot of a particle is shown in the figure, for a time interval of $40\text{ s}$. The total distance travelled by the particle and the average velocity during this period are, respectively _______.
questions.solution:
The total distance travelled by the particle is equal to the sum of the magnitudes of the areas under the velocity-time graph.

Area of the first triangle (from $t = 0$ to $t = 20\text{ s}$) is:
$A_1 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 20 \times 5 = 50\text{ m}$

Magnitude of the area of the second triangle (from $t = 20$ to $t = 40\text{ s}$) is:
$|A_2| = \left| \dfrac{1}{2} \times 20 \times (-5) \right| = 50\text{ m}$

Total distance $= A_1 + |A_2| = 50 + 50 = 100\text{ m}$

The total displacement is the algebraic sum of the areas under the velocity-time graph.

Total displacement $= A_1 + A_2 = 50 - 50 = 0\text{ m}$

Average velocity is the ratio of total displacement to total time.

Average velocity $= \dfrac{\text{Total displacement}}{\text{Total time}} = \dfrac{0}{40} = 0$

Answer: $100\text{ m}$ and zero

questions.q:
From $18$ m height above the ground a ball is dropped from rest. The height above the ground at which the magnitude of velocity equal to the magnitude of acceleration (in the same set of units) due to gravity is _____ m.
(Take $g = 10$ m/s$^2$ and neglect the air resistance)
questions.solution:
Let the ball fall a distance $s$ from the initial height.

Initial velocity $u = 0$

Acceleration $a = g = 10$ m/s$^2$

Given that the magnitude of velocity is equal to the magnitude of acceleration due to gravity, we have $v = 10$ m/s.

Using the equation of motion $v^2 = u^2 + 2gs$:

$(10)^2 = 0^2 + 2 \times 10 \times s$

$100 = 20s$

$s = 5$ m

The distance fallen by the ball is $5$ m.

The height above the ground is $h = H - s$

$h = 18 - 5 = 13$ m

Answer: $13$

questions.q: Two cars $A$ and $B$ are moving in the same direction along a straight line with speeds $100$ km/h and $80$ km/h, respectively such that car $A$ is moving ahead of car $B$. A person in car $B$ throws a stone with a speed $v$ so that it hits the car $A$ with a speed of $5$ m/s. The value of $v$ is ______ km/h.
questions.solution:
Velocity of car A, $v_A = 100$ km/h

Velocity of car B, $v_B = 80$ km/h

Velocity of the stone relative to car B is $v$. The velocity of the stone relative to the ground is $v_S = v_B + v = 80 + v$.

The velocity of the stone relative to car A is $v_{S/A} = v_S - v_A = (80 + v) - 100 = v - 20$.

The stone hits car A with a relative speed of $5$ m/s. Converting this speed to km/h:

$v_{S/A} = 5 \times \dfrac{18}{5} = 18$ km/h

Equating the relative speeds:

$v - 20 = 18 \Rightarrow v = 38$ km/h

Answer: $38$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The velocity of a particle is given as $\vec{v} = -x\hat{i} + 2y\hat{j} - z\hat{k}$ m/s. The magnitude of acceleration at point $(1, 2, 4)$ is _______ m/s$^2$.
questions.solution:
The velocity vector is given by $\vec{v} = v_x \hat{i} + v_y \hat{j} + v_z \hat{k} = -x \hat{i} + 2y \hat{j} - z \hat{k}$.

The components of acceleration are:

$a_x = v_x \dfrac{\partial v_x}{\partial x} + v_y \dfrac{\partial v_x}{\partial y} + v_z \dfrac{\partial v_x}{\partial z} = (-x)(-1) + 0 + 0 = x$

$a_y = v_x \dfrac{\partial v_y}{\partial x} + v_y \dfrac{\partial v_y}{\partial y} + v_z \dfrac{\partial v_y}{\partial z} = 0 + (2y)(2) + 0 = 4y$

$a_z = v_x \dfrac{\partial v_z}{\partial x} + v_y \dfrac{\partial v_z}{\partial y} + v_z \dfrac{\partial v_z}{\partial z} = 0 + 0 + (-z)(-1) = z$

The acceleration vector is $\vec{a} = x \hat{i} + 4y \hat{j} + z \hat{k}$.

At the point $(1, 2, 4)$, substituting $x = 1$, $y = 2$, and $z = 4$:

$\vec{a} = 1 \hat{i} + 4(2) \hat{j} + 4 \hat{k} = \hat{i} + 8 \hat{j} + 4 \hat{k}$

The magnitude of acceleration is:

$|\vec{a}| = \sqrt{1^2 + 8^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{1 + 64 + 16} = \sqrt{81} = 9$ m/s$^2$

Answer: $9$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A particle starts moving from time $t=0$ and its coordinate is given as $x(t)=4 t^{3}-3 t$
A. The particle returns to its original position (origin) 0.866 units later
B. The particle is 1 unit away from origin at its turning point
C. Acceleration of the particle is non-negative
D. The particle is 0.5 units away from origin at its turning point
E. Particle never turns back as acceleration is non-negative
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Given $x(t) = 4t^3 - 3t$, we find $v(t) = 12t^2 - 3$ and $a(t) = 24t$.
Statement A: Setting $x(t) = 0$ gives $4t^3 - 3t = 0 \Rightarrow t(4t^2-3) = 0$, so $t = 0$ or $t = \sqrt{3/4} = 0.866$. The particle returns to origin at $t = 0.866$ units. TRUE.
Statement B: Turning points occur at $v(t) = 0 \Rightarrow 12t^2 - 3 = 0 \Rightarrow t = \pm 0.5$. At $t = 0.5$: $x = 4(0.125) - 1.5 = -1$; distance = 1 unit. At $t = -0.5$: $x = 1$; distance = 1 unit. TRUE.
Statement C: For $t \geq 0$ (particle starts at $t=0$), $a(t) = 24t \geq 0$. TRUE.
Statement D: At turning points, distance is 1 unit, not 0.5. FALSE.
Statement E: False because acceleration is non-negative only for $t \geq 0$, and particle does turn back at $t = 0.5$. FALSE.
Correct statements: A, B, C Only.

questions.q:
Water drops fall from a tap on the floor, 5 m below, at regular intervals of time, the first drop strikes the floor when the sixth drop begins to fall. The height at which the fourth drop will be from ground, at the instant when the first drop strikes the ground is $\_\_\_\_$ m.
$\left(\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}\right)$
questions.solution:
Time for first drop to fall 5 m:
$5 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times t^2$ gives $t = 1$ s.
Since the first drop strikes when the sixth begins, there are 5 intervals: each interval $T = \frac{1}{5} = 0.2$ s.
When drop 1 hits the ground (at $t = 1$ s), drop 4 has been falling for $t_4 = 1 - 3 \times 0.2 = 0.4$ s.
Distance fallen by drop 4: $s_4 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times (0.4)^2 = 0.8$ m.
Height of drop 4 above ground: $5 - 0.8 = 4.2$ m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A paratrooper jumps from an aeroplane and opens a parachute after 2 s of free fall and starts deaccelerating with $3 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$. At 10 m height from ground, while descending with the help of parachute, the speed of paratrooper is $5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. The initial height of the airplane is $\_\_\_\_$ m.
$\left(\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}\right)$
questions.solution:
During the first $2\text{ s}$ of free fall, the paratrooper starts from rest ($u = 0$).
Velocity after $2\text{ s}$ is $v_1 = u + gt = 0 + 10 \times 2 = 20\text{ m/s}$.
Distance covered during free fall is $h_1 = \frac{1}{2}gt^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 2^2 = 20\text{ m}$.
After opening the parachute, the paratrooper decelerates at $a = -3\text{ m/s}^2$.
At a height of $10\text{ m}$ from the ground, the final velocity is $v_2 = 5\text{ m/s}$.
Let $h_2$ be the distance covered during deceleration until reaching $10\text{ m}$ height.
Using $v_2^2 = v_1^2 + 2ah_2$:
$5^2 = 20^2 + 2(-3)h_2$
$25 = 400 - 6h_2$
$6h_2 = 375$
$h_2 = 62.5\text{ m}$.
The total height of the airplane is the sum of the free fall distance, the deceleration distance, and the remaining height from the ground.
$H = h_1 + h_2 + 10 = 20 + 62.5 + 10 = 92.5\text{ m}$.

When the bullet just enters the target, its equation of motion is given by

${v}^{2} - {u}^{2} = 2aS . . . \left(1\right)$

Equation (1) implies that

${\left(\dfrac{2u}{3}\right)}^{2} = {u}^{2} + 2\left(- a\right)\left(4 \times {10}^{- 2}\right) ⇒ \dfrac{4{u}^{2}}{9} = {u}^{2} - 2a\left(4 \times {10}^{- 2}\right) ⇒ \dfrac{5{u}^{2}}{9} = 2a\left(4 \times {10}^{- 2}\right) \ldots \left(2\right)$

$0 = {\left(\dfrac{2u}{3}\right)}^{2} + 2\left(- a\right)\left(x\right) . . . \left(3\right)$

Equation (3) implies that

$\dfrac{4{u}^{2}}{9} = 2ax . . . \left(4\right)$

Dividing equation (2) by equation (4), we have

$\dfrac{5}{4} = \dfrac{4 \times {10}^{- 2}}{x} ⇒ x = \dfrac{16}{5} \times {10}^{- 2} ⇒ x = 3 . 2 \times {10}^{- 2}m = 32 \times {10}^{- 3}m$

Hence, $D = 32$.

questions.q: A horse rider covers half the distance with $5m{s}^{- 1}$ speed. The remaining part of the distance was travelled with speed $10m{s}^{- 1}$ for half the time and with speed $15m{s}^{- 1}$ for other half of the time. The mean speed of the rider averaged over the whole time of motion is $\dfrac{x}{7}m{s}^{- 1}$. The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution:
Let total distance travelled by horse rider be $2x$.

Now, the time taken to cover first half distance is ${t}_{AB} = \dfrac{x}{5}$

Second half distance $x$ between $BC$ is covered in two parts, $x = {d}_{1} + {d}_{2}$

here ${d}_{1}$ is the distance travelled with $10m{s}^{- 1}$ and ${d}_{2}$ is the distance travelled with $15m{s}^{- 1}$ in equal time intervals $\dfrac{t}{2}$ each.

Then, ${d}_{1} = \dfrac{10t}{2}, {d}_{2} = \dfrac{15t}{2}$

Second half distance $x = \dfrac{t}{2} ( 10 + 15 ) = \dfrac{25t}{2}$

Now, the mean speed of rider is $v = \dfrac{2x}{\dfrac{x}{5} + \dfrac{2x}{25}} = \dfrac{2 \times 25}{5 + 2} = \dfrac{50}{7}m{s}^{- 1}$

Thus, the value of $x = 50$.

$⇒ h = \dfrac{g}{2{n}^{2}}$

So, the balls rise up to a height of $h = \dfrac{g}{2{n}^{2}}m$.

questions.solution:
As the body is dropped from a certain height $h$, its initial velocity will be zero.

For first half, ${h}_{1} = \dfrac{h}{2}$.

Using second equation of motion, $s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}a{t}^{2}$

We have, $\dfrac{h}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}g{t}_{1}^{2}$.

Time taken in travel first half of the height, ${t}_{1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{h}{g}} . . . \left(1\right)$.

$h = \dfrac{1}{2}g{\left({t}_{1} + {t}_{2}\right)}^{2} ⇒ \left({t}_{1} + {t}_{2}\right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}} . . . \left(2\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{{t}_{1}}{{t}_{1} + {t}_{2}}$

$⇒ 1 + \dfrac{{t}_{2}}{{t}_{1}} = \sqrt{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{t}_{1}}{{t}_{2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2} - 1}$

Thus, the relation is ${t}_{2} = \left(\sqrt{2} - 1\right){t}_{1}$.

The height from the ground up to which the ball can rise will be $\left(\dfrac{k}{5}\right)m$. The value of $k$ is _____ (use $g = 9 . 8m{s}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
Initial velocity of ball is $u = 19 . 6m{s}^{- 1}$, final velocity $v = 0$.

Using $v = u + at$, here, acceleration $a = - g$.

Time taken in upward motion above tower is ${t}_{a} = \dfrac{u}{g} = \dfrac{19 . 6}{9 . 8} = 2s$

Now, time taken from top most point to ground is ${t}_{d} = 6 - 2 = 4s$.

Or, ${t}_{d} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2{h}_{max}}{g}}$ (Using $s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}g{t}^{2}$)

$⇒ {h}_{max} = \dfrac{16 \times 9 . 8}{2} = \dfrac{392}{5}m$.

Hence, the value of $k = 392$.

questions.q:
A NCC parade is going at a uniform speed of $9km{h}^{- 1}$ under a mango tree on which a monkey is sitting at a height of $19 . 6m$. At any particular instant, the monkey drops a mango. A cadet will receive the mango whose distance from the tree at time of drop is :
(Given $g = 9 . 8m{s}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
If a cadet receives the mango, then the time taken by the mango to fall and the cadet to reach there should be equal.

Time taken by mango to fall $t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}}$.

$⇒ t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 19 . 6}{9 . 8}} = 2s$

Therefore, the distance of the cadet from the tree will be, $d = vt$.

$⇒ d = 9 \times \dfrac{5}{18} \times 2 = 5m$

$⇒ {{v}_{0}}^{2} = 2\left(\dfrac{{{v}_{0}}^{2}}{9}\right)\left(4 + x\right)$

$⇒ 4 . 5 = 4 + x$

questions.q: A bullet is shot vertically downwards with an initial velocity of $100m{s}^{- 1}$ from a certain height. Within $10s$, the bullet reaches the ground and instantaneously comes to rest due to the perfectly inelastic collision. The velocity-time curve for total time $t = 20s$ will be : (Take $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
As the upward direction is taken as positive, the velocity at $t = 0$ is $u = - 100m{s}^{- 1}$.

As it is falling under gravity, its acceleration is constant and $a = - 10m{s}^{- 2}$.

Applying equation of motion for constant acceleration during the time of fall i.e., for $0$ to $10s$,

$v = u + at ⇒ v = - 100 - 10 \times 10 ⇒ v = - 200m{s}^{- 1}$

After $10s$ it hits the ground and remains at rest.

Therefore, option A is the correct representation.

questions.q: A car covers $AB$ distance with first one-third at velocity ${v}_{1}{ms}^{- 1}$, second one-third at ${v}_{2}{ms}^{- 1}$ and last one-third at ${v}_{3}{ms}^{- 1}$. If ${v}_{3} = 3{v}_{1}, {v}_{2} = 2{v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{1} = 11{ms}^{- 1}$, then the average velocity of the car is _____ ${ms}^{- 1}$.
questions.solution:
Let the total distance be $d$.

Time taken to cover ${\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{rd}$ of total distance is ${t}_{1} = \dfrac{d}{3{v}_{1}}$.

Time taken to cover ${\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{rd}$ of total distance is ${t}_{2} = \dfrac{d}{3{v}_{2}}$.

Time taken to cover ${\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{rd}$ of total distance is ${t}_{3} = \dfrac{d}{3{v}_{3}}$.

Average speed$= \dfrac{Totaldistance}{Totaltime}$

${v}_{avg} = \dfrac{d}{\dfrac{d}{3{v}_{1}} + \dfrac{d}{3{v}_{2}} + \dfrac{d}{3{v}_{3}}}$

$⇒ {v}_{avg} = \dfrac{3\left({v}_{1}{v}_{2}{v}_{3}\right)}{{v}_{1}{v}_{2} + {v}_{2}{v}_{3} + {v}_{3}{v}_{1}}$

Here, ${v}_{1} = 11m{s}^{- 1}$, then, ${v}_{3} = 33m{s}^{- 1}, {v}_{2} = 22m{s}^{- 1}$

${V}_{avg} = \dfrac{3 \times 11 \times 22 \times 33}{\left(11 \times 22\right) + \left(22 \times 33\right) + \left(33 \times 11\right)} = 18m{s}^{- 1}$

questions.solution:

Area of $\triangle O A B=S$ and $O B=t$. Let $O L=t_1$,
$\mathrm{LB}=\mathrm{t}_2$ and $\mathrm{AL}=\mathrm{v}, \mathrm{S}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{OB} \cdot \mathrm{AL}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{t} \cdot \mathrm{v} ; \mathrm{v}=\frac{2 \mathrm{~S}}{\mathrm{t}}$

questions.q: From a building two balls $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ are thrown such that $\mathrm{A}$ is thrown upwards $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ downwards (both vertically). If $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}}$ are their respective velocities on reaching the ground, then
options:
$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{B}}>\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{A}}$

$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{A}}=\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{B}}$

$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{A}}>\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{B}}$

their velocities depend on their masses
questions.solution:
As the ball moves down from height ' $h$ ' to ground the P.E at height ' $h$ ' is converted to K.E. at the ground (Applying Law of conservation of Energy)
Hence, $\frac{1}{2} m_A v_A^2=m_A g h_A$ or $v_A=\sqrt{2 g h_A}$; Similarly, $v_B=\sqrt{2 g h}$ or $v_A=v_B$

questions.q:
If a body looses half of its velocity on penetrating 3 cm in a wooden block, then how much will it
penetrate more before coming to rest?
questions.solution:
Let the initial velocity of the body be v. Hence the final velocity = v/2
Applying $v^2=u^2-2 a s \Rightarrow\left(\frac{v}{2}\right)^2=v^2-2 \cdot a \cdot 3 \Rightarrow a=v^2 / 8$
In IInd case when the body comes to rest, final velocity = 0, initial velocity = v/2
Again, $(0)^2=\left(\frac{v}{2}\right)^2-2 \cdot \frac{v^2}{8} \cdot s ;$ or $s=1 \mathrm{~cm}$
So the extra penetration will be $1 \mathrm{~cm}$
